output.brief:
I collected no further evidence, because what we already have points one way. The Level 2 potassium flag looks like a single chance outlier. A re-run of the same vial 21 minutes later passed. The Level 1 and Level 3 results and sodium and chloride were all in control. Potassium QC means are unchanged since the new reagent lot. All 182 scheduled QC runs were completed, so short staffing did not cause skipped QC. Analyzer B and Analyzer A agree on 43 re-run patient samples, within 0.10 mmol/L. So there is no sign of false highs or a systematic fault. The Ward 6 high results are split evenly between the two analyzers. They coincide with the tube outage, which brought longer transport times, and with four overflow renal patients, so those are the likelier explanations. Transport delay is a probable cause, not a proven one, and nobody has requested repeat samples.

What to sign off: return Analyzer B to potassium service and close the review of the 186 flagged results without amendments. I'm only moderately sure of this, so also run an extra Level 2 QC at the start of each shift for a week. Don't recall results, quarantine the lot or widen limits. Widening limits would blunt the control that caught this. Tell Ward 6 the analyzers are agreeing, and ask them to request repeat samples on their high results. Don't record a sampling glitch as the confirmed cause, because we can't tell it apart from chance.
